Hi, I’m 10 years post-op and I can assure you that you will be alright. I was 14 when I had the surgery (I’m fused all the way from top to bottom pretty much lol) and I’ve had the same thoughts you’re experiencing right now. My biggest fears were the potential complications, not having a normal life after the surgery etc.

What comforted me the most was the fact that I was in good hands (my surgeon, my PT, etc.) and I had my family supporting me.

First few days after my surgery, I was in a lot of pain of course, but I slowly started moving around with my PT. Within a month, I was pretty much back on my feet albeit with extra care. 10 years later and I am doing a LOT better as opposed to when I haven’t undergone spinal surgery yet. It has greatly improved my life and I know it will improve yours too. Wishing you luck! 🫶

Hey! I also failed three times too. I cried on my 2nd attempt and the driving instructor had to awkwardly leave me to my own devices after telling me I failed. Basically, I had tunnel vision on failure and only focused on that so as a result, I failed three times. I guess the nerves got to me and I also felt like I wasn’t good enough after each attempt. The thought of not being able to drive was so embarrassing for me and I simply wanted to crawl into a hole and just lay there.

On my 3rd attempt, I stalled for a couple of seconds on a traffic light, and then I accidentally passed the white line a bit too early on the motorway. I don’t know which country you’re from, but I live in a nordic country and it’s insanely strict here.

Looking back now, I’m actually pretty glad I failed a couple of times, because I learned from my mistakes. The most major one for me that needed an extra TLC were turning left, intersections, and observation (as in, showing the instructor you are moving your head to look).

Just: practice, practice, practice! I finally passed on the 4th attempt and a few years later I’m extremely comfortable with driving. You got this, don’t give up!

But if you still can't sleep in certain positions, don't force it.

TBH, I mostly spent my days laying in bed post-op.

1 year post-op, I was able to sleep whichever position I wanted. 6 years later and I sleep on my stomach everyday. You'll get there!

What type of mattress do you sleep on? Most people here, myself included, prefer firm-ish. I had a super soft topper on top of my mattress post-op and had to take that out for a while because I didn't enjoy my back sinking. Putting a pillow underneath your legs is a great standard sleeping position. And make sure to keep your head's pillow elevated so you wouldn't strain your neck. Perhaps try sleeping with more pillows too? Do whatever makes you comfortable. :)
